# Closure and Escalation Notes

**Suspicious Service Installation (PsExec-style / Command Services)** · `T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation` · [T1569.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/)

Fill in only what you checked. A confirmed attack is never closed from the queue: send the escalation note instead.

## Benign Positive

The rule fired on real activity that is expected and authorized.

```text
Alert:        T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation for <host> at <time, UTC>
Observed:     EventID=<value>  Provider_Name=<value>  ServiceName=<value>  ImagePath=<value>
Checked:      1. Review ServiceName, ImagePath, AccountName and Computer -> <result>
              2. Check whether ADMIN$ or a loopback share is involved -> <result>
              3. Find the network logon (4624 type 3) seconds before the 7045 -> <result>
              4. Check for change records or known admin PsExec usage -> <result>
Benign:       <which known source below> - confirmed by <change record, owner or ticket>
Disposition:  Benign Positive
Tuning:       none | defender_kernel_driver (applied) | psexec_service_name (rejected)
```

Known benign sources for this detection:
- Sysinternals PsExec used by administrators

Never tune:
- Never filter by service name or by LocalSystem: both are what attackers' tooling uses by default.

## False Positive

The rule matched something that is not the behaviour it describes.

```text

Disposition:  False Positive
Follow-up:    event sent to detection engineering as a true negative for T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation
```

## Escalation to incident response

```text
Alert:        T1569.002_suspicious_service_installation for <host> at <time, UTC>
Escalated:    <the condition met, from the list below>
Observed:     EventID=<value>  Provider_Name=<value>  ServiceName=<value>  ImagePath=<value>
Who / where:  <account> on <host>; source <host or address, if any>
Risk:         base 60 + <conditions met> = <score>
Preserved:    7045 event -> <where it is saved>
              Preceding 4624 type 3 and 5140/5145 share access -> <where it is saved>
              Service binary before it is deleted -> <where it is saved>
              Source host of the network logon -> <where it is saved>
Containment:  none yet | <action taken, time UTC>
Recommended:  Collect the service binary, delete the service, and investigate the source host as compromised
```

Escalate when any of these holds:
1. ImagePath runs cmd or PowerShell or lives under Temp, Public or AppData
2. Service name matches PsExec, PAExec, RemCom, CSExec or smbexec defaults, or an 8-letter random binary
3. No matching change or admin activity

Risk conditions: remote execution +15 · host is critical +20 · payload in user writable path +10 · approved admin activity -25 · approved change window -20.

Containment options, after the evidence above is preserved:
1. Collect the service binary
2. Delete the service
3. Treat the source host as compromised and investigate it
